doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Women trombonists and her future in New York
summary: They discuss women trombonists, a white woman with Ray Charles, Janice Robinson, and Liston's plans to find someone to help her play again.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Playing what?
Playing trombone.

Oh really? Oh please. I haven’t seen her. You just don’t see – there was one girl that was from ’Frisco that was playing with – that was playing in the band when they played your music at the conference. I can’t think of her name, but she was with Diva when they came out here, but I don’t think she’s with them now. I think she went back to school. But she was very good. And then there was a girl in Chicago was very good. She took some solos that night too on some of your music, and she was quite good. Out here on the West Coast, I don’t know of any. But if you said – is that girl with Ray Charles – is she from the West Coast?
No. She’s just playing jazz about two years, because she was playing symphony before that.
That’s what the girl in Chicago did too. She was – but she does both now, and she’s quite good. But I’ve got to check the girl out with Ray Charles.
She’s white. A white girl.
Is she?
He’s got three trombones.
You didn’t talk about Janice Robinson?
No. She was with me. She called me the other day.
Did she really?
She was talking about taking up the horn again.
She got married and put it down.
Yeah.
Such a beautiful trombonist.
I told her I was coming back there and I would call her when I came back there. I’m going to get somebody to – not teach me, but sit with me.
Right. Walk you through it, so you can get back to where you were.
I don’t know.
Try to get back to where you were. As long as you make the effort, there’s always a possibility of succeeding. In other words, your future will really begin when you get back to New York. You think?
Yeah, I guess so. Another phase of it, anyway.
